questions.q: Why does this project serve FactSales through a lakehouse SQL endpoint instead of standing up a separate Fabric Data Warehouse?
options: FactSales is already a well-modeled Delta table and the dashboard's queries are straightforward aggregations, so copying it into a separate warehouse adds no benefit
Fabric Data Warehouses cannot query star-schema tables
Lakehouses and warehouses are the same engine in Fabric, so the choice doesn't matter
A Data Warehouse is required whenever a dashboard is involved
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 11's lakehouse-vs-warehouse comparison favors the lakehouse SQL endpoint exactly when the data is already well-modeled and queries are simple aggregations.

questions.q: What does Fabric's Direct Lake mode actually do?
options: Reads a Delta table's Parquet files directly into a semantic model, skipping both a scheduled import and a live per-click query round-trip
Copies the entire Delta table into a new SQL database nightly
Requires exporting data to CSV before a dashboard can read it
Only works with Fabric Data Warehouses, never lakehouses
questions.explain: Direct Lake mode (Fabric Lesson 12) reads Delta/Parquet files directly, avoiding both import scheduling and DirectQuery's per-click cost.

questions.q: Why doesn't a fast serving layer guarantee a fresh dashboard?
options: The dashboard is only as fresh as the gold-layer pipeline feeding it — freshness is inherited from the ingestion/transformation schedule, not created by the serving layer
Serving layers always introduce their own multi-hour delay
Fast serving layers are always fresher regardless of the pipeline behind them
Freshness only matters for streaming sources, not batch ones
questions.explain: Online sales flow through in minutes and in-store sales land the next morning because of the ingestion schedule, not because of anything the serving layer does.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat the serving-layer choice as separate from Lesson 66's transformation/modeling decisions?
options: A well-modeled gold table can be served through more than one engine depending on the query pattern, so getting the serving choice wrong doesn't require redoing the modeling work
Serving and transformation are actually the same decision made twice
The serving layer must be decided before the star schema is designed
Separating the decisions has no practical benefit in this project
questions.explain: Lesson 15 makes this same point: modeling and serving are independent decisions, which is why choosing wrong on one doesn't force redoing the other.

questions.q: In the semantic model exposed to the dashboard, what role does FactSales play, and what are DimStore, DimProduct, and DimDate?
options: FactSales is marked as the fact table; DimStore, DimProduct, and DimDate are marked as dimensions, with relationships matching the foreign keys from the gold-layer design
All four tables are treated as facts with no dimensions defined
FactSales is a dimension and DimStore is the fact table
The semantic model ignores the star schema entirely and queries raw silver tables
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 13's semantic model layer exposes the star schema built in Lesson 66 directly to the dashboard tool.
